column30: Who can apply: "An undergraduate University degree in Engineering, Science, Informatics, Economics & Business Administration as well as from Technological Educational Institutes in related subject areas, in Greece or a recognized Higher Education Institution from abroad." Key-facts box: "An undergraduate degree from an accredited University, preferably in Engineering, Science, Informatics, Economics & Business Administration." No ECTS floor and no minimum number of years is published. Foreign institutions must be on the DOATAP recognised list, and enrolment requires an authenticated degree (validation via a Greek consulate/embassy, can take 3+ months). Greek first-cycle degrees are normally 4 years / 240 ECTS, but the programme publishes no credit minimum, so 180 ECTS is neither accepted nor excluded in writing.

column30: No ECTS or year threshold published - the requirement is expressed as level comparability assessed individually by the Board of Admissions. For applicants from a foreign research university: a "relevant bachelor's degree" from an institution "with a level similar to Dutch universities", with the Board verifying both content and level. Relevant fields are "such as, but not limited to, computer science, artificial intelligence, cognitive science, biology, design, mechanical engineering, or creative/performing arts". Substantive requirements: affinity and experience with fundamental and/or knowledge-driven research; affinity and experience with technology and its embedding in the human context; ability to think and reason beyond disciplinary borders; competence in imperative programming (C, C++, Java, Python); and mathematics covering algebra, functions, statistics, probability and distributions. No pre-master or bridging route is mentioned, so a shortfall means rejection rather than a bridging year.
